prices.shock:
An exfiltration of the account and transaction record store suppresses fee income for a quarter.
THE TRIPLE IS AN ANCHOR, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and it is graded 3 for exactly that reason. This institution has no incident of its own to measure, so the three numbers are arithmetic on a comparable UK challenger bank's own published regulatory record, nested from the narrowest reading to the widest:

  min  0.0640 = 28,959,426 / 452,800,000
  mode 0.0698 = 28,959,426 / 414,814,000
  max  0.0987 = 40,959,426 / 414,814,000

28,959,426 GBP is the financial penalty in the FCA's Final Notice against Starling Bank Limited of 2024-09-27 (reference 730166), and 40,959,426 GBP is the same notice's figure before the 30% stage-one settlement discount. 452,800,000 GBP is the revenue the same notice states at 2.1 for 2023; 414,814,000 GBP is Total Income for the year ended 2023-03-31 in that bank's own audited Annual Report 2023, a different metric on a different reporting convention. Sources and the discrepancy are recorded in the hub's .scratch/ecosystem/research/94-studied-firms.md.
What it is NOT: a conduct penalty is not a suppression of fee income, and that firm is not this one. Grade 3 on the published ladder is "an established mechanism from published work, not observed here", which is precisely the claim being made. Grade 3 is OUTSIDE the ladder's path_admission_threshold of 2, so no impact enters this perspective's pound through this edge and emit-forward-intel.py refuses to emit a priced payload while it is the only causal edge here. A grade-1 or grade-2 replacement is this institution's own dated incident record, and a regrade event has to record who moved it and why (twin/evidence.py).
